title: Beylik of Teke
capsule: The Beylik of Teke was an Anatolian Turkish principality centered on Antalya, established around 1321 by Yunus Bey of the Hamidid dynasty following the fragmentation of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum. It controlled the Pamphylian and Lycian coastlands of southern Anatolia and was one of several beyliks competing for influence in the post-Seljuk vacuum. The Ottomans first annexed the beylik in 1391, but Timur's Anatolian campaign of 1402 and the subsequent Ottoman collapse briefly restored local rule under Othman Chelebi. The Ottomans permanently reabsorbed Teke in 1423, incorporating it into their expanding state under Murad II.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The beylik's core territory around Antalya is well identified, but the exact extent of Teke control over interior Anatolian districts at different dates is uncertain given limited chronicle evidence.
